characters.name: Colonel K
characters.description: A chinchilla. The leader of the Danger Agency and Danger Mouse's boss. Batman Can Breathe in Space: In"The Other Day the Earth Stood Still", DM, Penfold and Colonel K all can. Broke Episode: The first episode"Danger Mouse Begins... Again"has shades of this after DM stops Panda-Minion. Colonel K tells DM point blank that the bill to repair London after the latter's pursuit of Panda-Minion had bankrupted the secret service to the point that Colonel K and P. Squawkencluck had to share their respective areas of the HQ in one room. Eat the Bomb: In"The Return of Danger K", there is an explosive carrot claimed to be "powerful enough to destroy a tank". Colonel K deals with it by swallowing it whole, and suffers no harm beyond a brief puff of smoke from his ears. Embarrassing Slide: In"Welcome to Danger World!", Colonel K accidentally shows DM and Penfold footage of himself doing aerobics instead of footage of the danger of the week.

characters.name: Danger Mouse
characters.description: A mouse. The world's greatest secret agent. AcCENT upon the Wrong SylLABle: One of DM's catchphrases was "You fiend", which he would inexplicably pronounce as "FEE-end." The Ace: His theme song even tells you outright! Danger Mouse and Jeopardy Mouse are tied for world's greatest secret agent (though they may have been bested by(Il) Hazard Mouse) and, despite hersusceptibility to bright lights, Danger Moth is the second greatest. Adaptation Personality Change: In the original series, DM was more sensible and collected. Here, DM is more of a Larger than life action hero. This may be due to the different pacing here, much faster. Added Alliterative Appeal: Gets called "the White Wonder".

characters.name: Ernest Penfold
characters.description: Added Alliterative Appeal: Gets called "the Hopeless Hamster". Attack of the 50-Foot Whatever: In"Chicken Run", Penfold grows to giant size after jumping into a feeder full of Professor Squawkencluck's growth serum. He winds up being the episode's hero as a result, capturing Greenback and Stiletto in the process. Bad "Bad Acting":At the beginning of"The Four Tasks of Danger Mouse", Greenback reveals to Danger Mouse that he is behind Penfold's kidnapping, and shows him a live feed of Penfold in his cell. Penfold claims he is being treated well, but the fact that he makes this claim in an awkward, wooden monotone clearly indicates that he is just saying what he has been told to say (if the occasional prompting from Greenback wasn't enough of a giveaway):Danger Mouse:Penfold! Are you all right?Penfold:(monotone)I'm - being - treated - well.Greenback:Good, good!Penfold:(still monotone)The frost in my cell is very pretty, I am not hungry anyway, and, erm, erm...Greenback:And the beetles!Penfold:Oh yes.And the beetles are awfully friendly.In the last act of"The Duel"after Penfold has been hypnotized by "Madame Stiletto" — not just monotone, but also in "Madame's" fake Roma accent:Penfold:I want-a to go-a for a ride on-a Big Dipper.DM:Yes, yes, alright, we'reonthe Big Dipper!Penfold:An' I-a will not-a tell-a you... it is-a a trap!DM:Alright! Then don't!DM and Penfold do the opening of"Bandits, Beans And Ballyhoo"after the narrator storms off. Their dialogue is delivered hammily and slowly.DM:(gestures to the lift)Come on, erm... Penfold, my faithful assistant!Penfold:(clears throat)I'm coming, Danger Mouse. 'Cor, it's nice to be back in the Mayfair headquarters of the world's greatest secret agent!(he indicates DM, who mugs at the camera and shows off his badge)DM:Yes. Although that holiday in Mexico was most enjoyable.(Penfold shows the "Mexico" label on their luggage)Penfold:Yes. It certainly was, Danger Mouse. At the beginning of"The Four Tasks of Danger Mouse", Greenba

characters.name: Flying Officer Buggles Pigeon
characters.description: Big Damn Heroes: Buggles is this for both"Chicken Run"and"Ice Station Camel", respectively getting Danger Mouse out of a pickle by carrying him (and Penfold in the first case) to safety. Continuity Nod: When DM explains Buggles' role in helping destroy Greenback's world-slowing machine in"Ice Station Camel", he helps jog Penfold's memory about him by mentioning that he helped during the "giant chicken case". Got Me Doing It: In"Chicken Run", the character of Flying Officer Buggles Pigeon is a parody of the stereotypical upper class RAF officer, and his Verbal Tic of ending sentences with "what?" is both confusing and, apparently, contagious:Buggles:Good show, what?Penfold:What?Buggles:What?Penfold:You said "what".Buggles:No, you said "what".Penfold:(irritated)Becauseyou... said "what".Buggles:'' Hm? Jolly confusing, what?—->DM:What? (groans) Oh, this- I'm at it now!

characters.name: Agent  57
characters.description: Legacy Character: Agent 57's son is Agent 58 in the reboot. Inexplicably Identical Individuals: In"The Spy Who Stayed In With A Cold", Agent 57 turns himself into DM as DM himself is held hostage by the Motorized Mongols. Involuntary Shapeshifting: Becomes able to change into any character or animal whenever he sneezes in"The Spy Who Stayed In With A Cold". Master of Disguise: Agent 57, who appears as a worm in his first appearance and a polar bear in his second. According to DM, he's disguised himself as so many things over the years that he's forgotten what his original species was. Meaningful Name: It's been said that master of disguise Agent 57 was so named as a reference to the Heinz company and its "57 varieties."

characters.name: Professor Heinrich Squawkencluck
characters.description: Gratuitous Foreign Language: Uses german words like "nein" while speaking english. Herr Doktor: He's a German scientist. Hurricane of Puns: In"Turn Of The Tide", Professor Squawkencluck gets frustrated with an explanation of what's caused the ocean to submerge London and started screaming some amount of "Nein, nein, nein!" Whenever he did, Penfold would be nearby with a calculator, reading off the total of the "nines". Nephewism: P. Squawkencluck from the reboot is Heinrich's niece. Non-Indicative Name: He"s actually a mole.

characters.name: Baron Silas Greenback
characters.description: Added Alliterative Appeal: Gets called "the Terrible Toad". Be Careful What You Wish For: After DM causes the Mega-Brain computer to blow up in"Mechanised Mayhem", it eventually stops Greenback's travel device from attacking their HQ. Greenback wants a bigger and better computer, and the Mega-Brain computer crash lands on top of him and Stiletto.Stiletto:Oh, well...it-a could been worse, Barone.Greenback:How worse, you dolt?Stiletto:Well, ya coulda wanted the Q.E. II!(they both laugh, but then they hear a steamship horn; they glance up,groan "Oh, no!"as the Q.E. II lands on top of them) Big Bad: Danger Mouse's archenemy who was in almost every episode of the first five seasons. Borrowed Catch Phrase: In the original series episode"The Ultra Secret Secret", it's Greenback who tells Penfold to shush, and DMobjects. Call-Back: In"Penfold Transformed, Greenback plants Stiletto in a Penfold costume with Danger Mouse and refers to the mistake he made creating too many in"Tiptoe Through The Penfolds".

characters.name: Stiletto Mafiosa
characters.description: Accent Adaptation: In the original broadcast he had an Italian accent, but when the show was handed over to Nickelodeon in America, he was redubbed with a Cockney accent. The DVD set by A&E gives him back the Italian accent, which is quite a surprise to people who grew up on the Nickelodeon cartoons. A few of Stiletto's lines were changed as well- as seen in "Public Enemy No. 1" after DM suffers his amnesia-inducing bump to the head, there is this exchange:Stiletto:All right...I am surrendered!DM:Hmmm? Oh...how do you do, Mr. Surrendered.Stiletto:Eh? Is that-a English joke, signor? (In America with Stiletto's accent change, the line was changed to "Don't you know who I am, guv?") Be Careful What You Wish For: After DM causes the Mega-Brain computer to blow up in"Mechanised Mayhem", it eventually stops Greenback's travel device from attacking their HQ. Greenback wants a bigger and better computer, and the Mega-Brain computer crash lands on top of him and Stiletto.Stiletto:Oh, well...it-a could been worse, Barone.Greenback:How worse, you dolt?Stiletto:Well, ya coulda wanted the Q.E. II!(they both laugh, but then they hear a steamship horn; they glance up,groan "Oh, no!"as the Q.E. II lands on top of them) Conspicuous Trenchcoat: He always wears a classic trenchcoat and fedora, as befits a shady villain for a secret organization. Demoted to Extra: Alongside Greenback and Nero, Stiletto was in nearly every episode for the first five seasons. Starting with season 6, they began to appear less in favor of more villains for Danger Mouse to face. The Dragon: To Baron Greenback.

characters.name: Nero
characters.description: A Day in the Limelight: After Greenback's scheme is accidentally ruined before it even begins in "Nero Power", Nero is the one that antagonises DM and Penfold for the majority of the episode, with powers gained as a result of Greenback's missile's destruction. Demoted to Extra: Nero, alongside Greenback and Stiletto, was in nearly every episode for the first five seasons. Starting with season 6, they began to appear less in favor of more villains for Danger Mouse to face. Ridiculously Cute Critter: Despite his evil personality and affiliation, Nero is a very fluffy and cute little guy. Right-Hand Cat: Nero's a... furry caterpillar-thing, but it's obvious what trope he's invoking.

characters.name: Leatherhead
characters.description: Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Only ever appeared in the pilot, its remake and two other episodes of the main series. Fat and Skinny: He is a roly-poly contrast to the very skinny Stiletto. The Slacker: He spends the majority of his screentime reading a comic book instead of aiding the Baron's schemes.

characters.name: Count Duckula
characters.description: A duck. He's obsessed with fame and wants to appear in television. Anvil on Head: In "From Duck to Dawn", Count Duckula attempts to drop a safe on DM. Attention Whore: Duckula got jealous of the negative attention Danger Mouse was getting from an angry mob planning to kill him, simply because they were trying to kill him while Duckula was performing. Biting-the-Hand Humor: When hekidnaps the writers, they are revealed to bemonkeys with typewriters.Duckula:What? What were you expecting? It's not like they're writing Shakespeare! Camera Abuse: At the end of "From Duck to Dawn", Count Duckula transforms into a bat and flies off, shouting a Medium-Aware We Will Meet Again boast back at DM — and then flies straight into the camera because he's not watching where he's going.

characters.name: Grovell
characters.description: A.I. Is a Crapshoot: Fits this to a tee.Quark:Jangs, when I find the idiot what programmed you...

characters.name: The Narrator
characters.description: Added Alliterative Appeal: He frequently lampshades the show's frequent use of this:"London, a city shrouded in shadows. From Shoreditch to Shooters hill, from Shaftesbury Street to Shepherds Bush, shoppers shrink as shady shapes shuffle shiftily. Who can shatter the sinister shutters? Shout for the nation's shield!Shend for Dangermoushe!" Cliffhanger: The stories in Series 2-4 aired in five minute segments every weekday. The first four episodes generally ended with a cliffhanger over aTo Be Continuedscreen, and at the beginning of the next day's episode, the narrator would deliver aPreviously on…to remind viewers where they were the previous day. For example, Episodes 4 and 5 of"Close Encounters of the Absurd Kind"are bridged by a scene in which Penfold is sucked out of the airlock of a spaceship:Narrator:(at the end of Episode 4)Is Penfold destined to be the first Penfold togo where no Penfold has gone before?Can Danger Mouse get him back? Can our heroes escape from their alien captors? Will the guard lose his no-claim bonus on his hoverpod? And whereisBaron Greenback? To find out, tune in next time to Danger Mouse in"Close Encounters of the Absurd Kind"!(at the beginning of Episode 5)Colonel K warns Danger Mouse that the evil Baron Greenback is out to steal the Big Ear tracking station. But as he tries to seek out the evildoers, Penfold disappears in midair! About to be destroyed by Greenback's missile, Danger Mouse is sucked miraculously out of its path, and held prisoner by the strange creatures who idiotnapped Penfold. Mistakenly believing that they have been captured by the Baron, our heroes escape their captors, but while searching for a door to the outside, are once more parted! Will they ever meet again? Stay tuned for Part 5 of"Close Encounters of the Absurd Kind"! Description Cut: The Narrator frequently does this: From the opening of"Dream Machine":Narrator:Springtime in England, on a day unlike any other.(a sparkling green cloud floats over the Houses

characters.name: In General
characters.description: Child Soldier: Young Danger Agents who are being trained up to join the Danger Agency once they reach the appropriate level of physical and psychological maturation. Deus ex Machina: During the episodeThe Cute Shall Inherit the Earth, they function as Danger Mouse's tools for defeating the sinister cat cult, simply by "out-cuting" them and cancelling their adorability out. DM then delivers an insulting dig at the cult leader to add the icing to the cake: "The prophecy was right. It just wasn't about you." Flat Character: Beyond the fact that they're cute, nothing much is shown about them as individuals. Parental Abandonment: Nothing is shown of their parents or whatever happened to them. Presumably, their parents gave them away to the Danger Agency in exchange for a sum of money. Spin-Off Babies: Presumably they're a parody of this trope, since they're young Danger Agents who are essentially juvenile counterparts to the older members of the agency.

characters.name: Penfold
characters.description: A hamster. Danger Mouse's reluctant sidekick. Adaptation Personality Change: In the original series, Penfold was almost always cowardly. Here, Penfold is more courageous, and not as fearful as before, bordering on anInformed Attribute, but he still has his frightful moments. This may be due to the different pacing here, much faster. Added Alliterative Appeal: Gets called "the Hopeless Hamster". The Atoner: Parodied in"Escape from Big Head", where Penfold tearfully relates the lengths he went to to atone for the hideous crime of borrowing a pencil and forgetting to give it back. Attack of the 50-Foot Whatever:"Big Penfold"deals with the effects of a size-changing device on... well, the clue's in the title.

characters.name: Professor P. Squawkencluck
characters.description: A chicken. She creates the agency's tech. Cute, but Cacophonic: Sometimes lapses into this when she raises her voice. It's best seen in"The Unusual Suspects", when she's admonishing Danger Mouse and Penfold for popping the bubble wrap the Formula X they're delivering is concealed in.Squawkencluck:Remember- Formula X is a powerful weapon, and must not fall into the wrong hands-[DM and Penfold are ignoring her, and popping sheets of the bubble wrap]Squawkencluck:WHAT ARE YE DOING?!Penfold:[Still ignoring her]It's hard to stop, isn't it?Danger Mouse:I could literally do thisall day.Squawkencluck:[Shrieking]DANGER MOOOOOOUSE! Embarrassing First Name: As revealed in "Frankensquawk's Monster", "Professor" is her literal first name; DM is quite amused to learn this, to Squawk's annoyance. Furry Female Mane: She's one of the few characters (most of whom are also women) to have hair. Hartman Hips: Has wide hips and her bottom is noticeably much fatter than her slim upper body.

characters.name: Danger Moth
characters.description: Attention Deficit... Ooh, Shiny!: Naturally, being a moth, this is herFatal Flaw. Big Creepy-Crawlies: A large moth who is apparently large enough to have proper conversations with the rest of the heroes. Moth Menace: Averted. She's a moth, but she's definitely on the side of the heroes.

characters.name: Danger Mackerel
characters.description: Terrestrial Sea Life: Despite being a mackerel, he doesn't seem to have any trouble living on land.

characters.name: Danger Mole
characters.description: Artistic License – Biology: He's depicted as having fully-functioning eyes. Moles in real life are blind. Flat Character: Much like the other Danger Agents, his personality isn't fully developed other than the fact that he works on the Night Shift alongside Danger Moth.

characters.name: Danger Bug
characters.description: Multi-Armed and Dangerous: Being six-limbed, Danger Bug has two pairs of hands.

characters.name: Danger Snake
characters.description: Flat Character: Due to the fact that he only appears as a background character in one episode. Snakes Are Sinister: Averted. He's a snake, but he's working for the good guys.

characters.name: Danger Sheep
characters.description: Artistic License – Biology: Given that sheep are female and that rams are male, then heshouldbe a ram,nota sheep. If he is a ram, then he lacks the horns. Being Good Sucks: He realises this after seeing the Baron's domicile. Evil Is Cool: He comes to this conclusion upon witnessing just how glamorous Baron Greenback'sSupervillain Lairis. Face–Heel Turn: Originally on the side of good, he ends up defecting towards the side of the Baron upon being tempted by the life of luxury that comes with a lifestyle of supervillainy. Fatal Flaw: Several: he's arrogant and entitled, to the extent that he finds no point in doing good for its own sake.

characters.name: Agent  58
characters.description: A mimic octopus. He's the son of Agent 57 from the original series. Green-Eyed Monster: He attempts to sabotage DM and Penfold's relationship and replace the latter, only to turn hostile when rejected. Odd Name Out: His codename is doesn't share the theme every other Danger Agent's does.

characters.name: Norman
characters.description: A dog. He works in Danger Agency's IT support. Being Good Sucks: To a lesser extent than Danger Sheep. Despite the fact that he's a nice chap, he's often looked down upon by the other members of the Danger Agency, to the point where it is generally conceded that nobody would ever want to be him. Nice Guy: Despite his lack of popularity, he is indeed quite nice.

characters.name: Felicity
characters.description: An elephant. Colonel K's secretary. Honorable Elephant: An elephant who works on the side of the heroes.

characters.name: Danger Ellie
characters.description: A Lizard Named "Liz": Ellie is an elephant. Odd Name Out: All the other Danger Babies are only known by species names, like the agents. Then there's Ellie. It could theoretically be short for "Elephant" though.

characters.name: Danger Piglet
characters.description: Flat Character: Again, like the other Danger Babies, his personality isn't significantly developed. Housepet Pig: An anthropomorphic version of this trope. Sinister Swine: Averted, he's on the side of the heroes.

characters.name: Danger Foal
characters.description: Big Anime Eyes: He has a pair of these, adding to his adorability. Cool Horse: A juvenile version of this trope. Flat Character: Much like the other Danger Babies, his personality isn't developed beyond being cute.

characters.name: Danger Chick
characters.description: Cool Shades: She wears a futuristic version of these. Flat Character: Justified in that she's a child and hasn't properly developed a personality.

characters.name: Danger Puppy
characters.description: Flat Character: Much like the other Danger Babies, his personality isn't significantly developed beyond his over-the-top innocent adorability. No Name Given: We don't know his real name prior to his assignment of his title, if he even has one at all. Precious Puppy: As a member of the Danger Agency, he already is one.

characters.name: Jeopardy Mouse
characters.description: A mouse. Works for the Danger Agency's American equivalent. She has also infiltrated Hydrant using the name Red Fox, during which she disguises as a fox. Always Someone Better: Being funded by the US government, she has cooler toys than the British-funded Danger Mouse. When JM wants DM to cover for her so she can take Thanksgiving off, DM insists they get to use her toys as part of the deal. Distaff Counterpart: A female mouse who's also the greatest secret agent in the world. Not So Above It All: Isn't above having fun on her missions as well. The Rival: She's also "The greatest secret agent in the world", and whenever she has to work with Danger Mousethe two can't help trying to one-up each other.

characters.name: Hazard Mouse
characters.description: A mouse. He's a secret agent for the Italian government, and the equivalent to Danger Mouse and Jeopardy Mouse.

characters.name: Cupcake
characters.description: A clown alien from the planet Bozoria. She's a secret agent working for Crumples. Afro Hair: She has the standard multicoloured variant which is common for clowns to wear in fiction. Fatal Flaw: Her pride and arrogance. Patriotic Fervor: She is very attached to her homeworld and will not take to people insulting or belitting it. The Smurfette Principle: The only female Bozorian to ever appear in the series.

characters.name: Danger Cash
characters.description: An alien from Midas 7 who's made of money and diamonds.

characters.name: Danger Toad
characters.description: A toad. Silas von Greenback's good twin from theTwystyverse. Good Counterpart: To Baron Greenback.

characters.name: Crumples
characters.description: A clown alien from planet Bozoria. He's the previous president whom Pom Pom overthrows. Sometimes he's also a clown performer on Earth. All-Loving Hero: You could argue that he is this. He very quickly forgives Pom Pom for deposing him. Foil: He's one to Pom Pom, given that he's more open-minded about comedy and laughter than his rival. Married to the Job: He is this to the extent that he slipped into depression after he was overthrown. Nice Guy: Good, kind and humble to a fault.

characters.name: Baron von Greenback
characters.description: A toad. Danger Mouse's archenemy. Adaptational Nationality: Changed from British to German, complete with getting "von" added to his name. Adaptation Name Change: This show adds "von" to Greenback's name because he's German now. Added Alliterative Appeal: Gets called "the Terrible Toad". Ambiguous Situation: HisAdaptational Nationalitycalls into question whether he's an actual aristocrat given Germany abolished their nobility.

characters.name: Pandaminion
characters.description: A panda. He's Von Greenback's newest, lazy minion. Animal Stereotypes: Naturally, being a panda, he's lazy. Punny Name: Pandemonium. Simpleton Voice: He speaks with one on the few occasions where hedoes.

characters.name: Safety Mouse
characters.description: A robot mouse. Von Greenback created it for a plot. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: Ostensibly, it was created to save people and to replace Danger Mouse, butin reality, it was designed to kidnap the world's most important people. Job-Stealing Robot: The Safety Mice become this for secret agents and bodyguards, and they become a problem for Danger Mouse in particular since the only job he feels capable of performing to the utmost efficiency happens to be saving the world. Made of Iron: The Safety Mouse is constructed of a fictional material known as Convenientium, which is so strong that nothing can break through it.When Danger Mouse tries to attack it after it kidnaps the Queen, he ends up getting hurt pretty badly. Robot Police: On the surface, it seems the Safety Mouse was programmed to be one. During the advert for it which appears on television, it mercilessly beats up Stilletto before imprisoning him inside its portable prison.

characters.name: Redfield
characters.description: A giant red beetroot with eyes, a beak, two arms, and two legs. He's Duckula's minion. Brainwashed and Crazy: Implied due to how Duckula was depicted as turning people into vegetables in his debut episode. Early-Installment Weirdness: When Redfield is first introduced he is able to speak just fine, but all of his subsequent appearances have him asThe Voiceless. Shout-Out: Just like Duckula, Redfield is another reference to Bram Stoker'sDraculanovel - in this case the insane human Renfield that Dracula employs as an agent to act during the daytime whilst he sleeps.

characters.name: Quark
characters.description: Aliens Are Bastards: Only cares about profit above all else, which is why he loses it when Penfold leads the others into a thumb war and threatens to paint the Earth white and use it as a ball in a game of intergalactic ping-pong. Belly Mouth: He has one, and it speaks with a deeper voice and has a blunter personality that the one in his head. Cover Innocent Eyes and Ears: After Von Greenback accidentally drops his pants in front of Quark, Pandaminion, and Dawn, Quark puts a hand over Dawn's eyes (before covering his own eye with the other pair). Multi-Armed and Dangerous: He has one normal pair of hands on his torso, but also a smaller pair on his cheeks. Sharing a Body: Quark and his stomach mouth seem to be separate consciousnesses.

characters.name: Quark's Tummy
characters.description: A second mouth in Quark's stomach which talks and has its own personality. Catchphrase: "No refunds."

characters.name: Augustus P. Crumhorn IV
characters.description: A doberman. He's a billionaire industrialist CEO of Crumhorn Inc. and the father of Dawn Crumhorn. Presumably the son of Doctor Augustus P. Crumhorn III from the original series. Corrupt Corporate Executive: Runs Crumcorp and is often trying to extend his reach of the world through buying and controlling everything he doesn't already own. This includes a popular social media platform and video game that characters like Penfold use on a daily basis. Doting Parent: He will go to any lengths to satisfy his daughter's demands, including unknown supernatural means to purchase a sacred Mayan calendar designed to remove certain days from the week. Evil Is Petty: If something he uses becomes faulty , say a lightbulb or orange, he makes plans to buy as many companies distributing them as possible to either hike up their prices or shut them down. Fiction 500: Easily the wealthiest character in the entire series, and possibly the world, on account of the giant conglomerate company he both operates and owns.

characters.name: Dawn "The Princess" Crumhorn (aka Pink Dawn/Dark Dawn)
characters.description: A poodle who won a tour through the Danger Agency, but being frequently denied access to dangerous gadgets soured her into a life of villainy. She is the daughter of an evil businessman named Augustus P. Crumhorn IV. Amazing Technicolor Population: For some reason, her fur is purplish pink. Daddy's Little Villain: Her father gives her everything she wants, so she's entitled to expect everyone else to do the same. Otherwise, she'll commit schemes to get it herself. Expy: She's the reboot's equivalent of Sweetie Pie from the original series, who was actually Crumhorn in disguise. Gender Equals Breed: Since her father is a dobermann (possibly part wolf too) but Dawn looks exactly like a poodle, she must have gotten her appearance from her never-seen mother.

characters.name: Mr. Snuggles
characters.description: A toy bear. He was Dawn Crumhorn's favourite toy, and she gave him sentience when she got her powers. Living Toys: He's a teddy bear magically brought to life. Vengeful Abandoned Toy: He becomes this when Dawn becomes Dark Dawn and decides she's had enough of him, which leads him to go on a destructive rampage through London.Eventually he and Dark Dawn reconcile, during which Dawn reverts to Pink Dawn again, her age apparently reduced to who she was before, and they happily leave.

characters.name: Rainbow Ponies
characters.description: A group of copies of Naughty Pony. Mr. Snuggles used them as his minions. Living Toys: They're toy ponies brought to life. Take That!: Presumably they're a jab at the My Little Pony toy brand.

characters.name: Birch Badboy
characters.description: A squirrel. He was a kind scientist working for the Danger Agency, until a time-traveling accident turned him into a rude punk. Delinquent: He is one, even in middle-age. Inexplicably Tailless: Averted. As a squirrel, he has an appropriately bushy tail. Nonconformist Dyed Hair: Has a green and purple mohawk. Older Than They Look: Considering the cold open of his debut episode was set during the 1980s, he's probably much older than he looks, somewhere in his forties at least.

characters.name: Ivana The Invisible
characters.description: Heinous Hyena: A hyena who works as one of the antagonists. Invisibility: She's invisible and rarely seen even by the audience. Her invisibility does have its limits, however, as she can become visible if sprayed with paint or covered with snow and she appears not to have any control over her invisibility powers. However, as with so many other mysteries present within this series, we don't really get an explanation for how she attained her powers. Invisible Jerkass: She's invisible and she's definitely a villain. However, similarly to H.G. Wells'Griffin, her invisibility appears to be deconstructed, as it would seem she has become permanently invisible. Invisible Streaker: Averted. Despite the fact that she's invisible, due to the fact that this is a children's show, in the few moments we see her transparent astral form, we never behold her as naked. Russian Guy Suffers Most: She appears to endure a lot of embarrassing defeats.

characters.name: Tutancowmoo
characters.description: A bull. Also a mummified pharaoh. Nepharious Pharaoh: He was a pharaoh in ancient Egypt. Non-Indicative Name: He's male, so he's not a cow but a bull. Punny Name: His name is a pun on Tutankhamun.

characters.name: The Cats
characters.description: Cats Are Mean: They're part of a mad cult intent on conquering the world. Cult: They're a deranged cult of fanatics, whose mantra is "The cute shall inherit the earth" (obviously a warped rendition of the Biblical adage of "The meek shall inherit the earth.") Take Over the World: This is their main goal, as exemplified by their mantra quoted above.

characters.name: Delilah von Greenback
characters.description: A toad. She's Silas's daughter. Furry Female Mane: Despite being a reptile, she has a full head of hair. Identical Grandson: Bears a striking resemblance to her father. Missing Mom: Her mother isn't around and never gets mentioned. Non-Standard Character Design: Her and her father's eyes are yellow instead of white like everybody else from the main universe. However, it's justified as toads really do have yellow eyes.

characters.name: Dr. Loocifer
characters.description: A high-tech toilet from Japan that was accidentally made sentient. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: An AI toilet who becomes sentient when Penfold accidentally tosses a computer chip into his basin. Afterwards he becomes self-aware and kickstarts a revolution of toilets, where they demand equal rights. Animate Inanimate Object: An AI toilet which was granted sentience. While he wasn't brought to life with magic, he is still a living toilet with his own thoughts and feelings. Berserk Button: Whenever someone uses his original name, John. When Danger Mouse uses the name, he loses his temper and unleashes the Portaloo to devour them. The Bus Came Back: In the episode where Quark is first introduced, he appears as one of the enemies Danger Mouse and Penfold have to fight on the desolate planet.

characters.name: Dudley Poyson
characters.description: Mad Doctor: As with his original counterpart, he is one of these. Ominous Owl: As with the original character, he is an owl who works as a villain. Punny Name: His name is a pun on the phrase "deadly poison".

characters.name: Mac The Fork
characters.description: The Cameo: Reduced to a non-vocal cameo in the reboot. Dastardly Dapper Derby: As with his original counterpart, Mac the Knife wears one, although it's a much lighter shade of blue than the original purple. Shout-Out: His name is a reference toMac The Knife. Snakes Are Sinister: He's a snake who happens to be one of the villains.

characters.name: Elon Musktrat
characters.description: A rat. He's a billionaire inventor. Ambiguous Situation: If Von Greenback was stealing his identity, or if there was never a real Elon Musktrat. No Celebrities Were Harmed: He's obviously a parody of Elon Musk. Non-Indicative Name: He doesn't look like a muskrat. Sinister Schnoz: He has a snout version of this.

characters.name: Frankensquawk's Monster
characters.description: A rooster / giant mutant rubbish monster. He's actually P. Squawkencluck's father, accidentally turned into a monster by his wife. Frankenstein's Monster: A parody of this character archetype. Karmic Transformation: While the transformation was accidental, it was nevertheless an appropriate punishment for his squalid and slobbish mannerisms. Thus, his wife altered his DNA so that waste would naturally attach itself to him, but this ended up going too far, causing him to become transformed into the bizarre refuse monster he is by the time the episode starts. Luke, I Am Your Father:He's actually the Professor's father, turned into a monster by his wife. Non-Indicative Name: Despite being named in reference to Frankenstein's monster, his creator does not bear the surname of Frankensquawk.

characters.name: Headless Postman
characters.description: Species unclear. A vengeful ghost. The Ghost: Never appears on-screen. Going Postal: He was a spectral postman, and he takes great delight in torturing people. Headless Horseman: A parody of this trope, and specifically a parody of this trope as it is depicted in Washington Irving'sThe Legend of Sleepy Hollow.

characters.name: Ian the Danger Fan
characters.description: A corgi. He's a fan of Danger Mouse, but becomes obsessive. Enfant Terrible: He's already a fairly sadistic and manipulative little brat at the age of ten years old. Fatal Flaw: He has two: firstly, his intense materialism, which drives him to collect any and all Danger Mouse memorabilia at any cost; secondly, the fact that he's dim-witted and easily fooled. These are flaws which Danger Mouse exploits in his debut episode. Heel–Face Turn: After an entire episode of being abused and mistreated by Crumhorn, he finally regrets his actions and helps DM and Penfold escape before destroying the missiles. Incredible Shrinking Man: He does this with all the villains DM has captured over the years, turning them into bizarre trophies.He later gets shrunk down himself.

characters.name: Isambard King Kong Brunel
characters.description: A monkey. He's a mad scientist with a Napoleon complex, which he compensates for by wearing an overly tall hat. Compensating for Something: Much like the real-life Kingdom Brunel, he has a very tall top hat, presumably to compensate for his short height. Early-Installment Weirdness: In his debut episode, where a comet is about to hit the Earth, he doesn't really come across as evil, and instead works with the other scientists to find ways to deter the comet. However the machine he proposes to use against the comet is nowhere near strong enough to deter it completely, instead only being capable of redirecting it to a location so that that particular location is destroyed first. Half-Dressed Cartoon Animal: One of the reboot's few examples. He forgoes pants and shoes and only wears a hat and a vest. Inexplicably Tailless: Averted. He has a tail befitting his species.

characters.name: Frankenstein's Rooster
characters.description: A rooster with a whisk for a head. It's a creation of Isambard King Kong Brunel, resenting him for releasing it into the wild in his island. However, it wants to protect the island. Hybrid Monster: A bizarre hybrid of rooster and egg whisk. Non Animal Head: It has a whisk for a head. Token Heroic Orc: Despite being a bizarre hybrid created by aMad Scientist, the creature attaches itself to Danger Mouse and Penfold, in contrast to its more menacing relative. Turned Against Their Masters: It absolutely despises Brunel for abandoning it on the island to fend for itself, in contrast to its intended purpose (which was to serve eggs in the morning).

characters.name: Tyrannotour-bus Rex
characters.description: A T Rex with a wheelless two-storey bus for a head and a wheel in the place of each hindleg. It was also created by Brunel and also lives on his island. Animal-Vehicle Hybrid: A bizarre hybrid between a tyrannosaurus rex and a bus. Non-Animal Head: As with its counterpart, it has its head replaced by something else — in this case, a common-or-gardenLondon transport diesel-engine 97-horsepower omnibus. Non-Indicative Name: Despite its name, its head bears a resemblance to a London double-decker bus rather than the conventional tour bus which musical groups are wont to travel in. Riddle for the Ages: Why was it created?

characters.name: Anagondola
characters.description: Animal-Vehicle Hybrid: Half snake, half Venetian gondola.

characters.name: Big Head
characters.description: An AI created by P. Squawkencluck, designed to keep Danger Mouse out of his headquarters. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: Big Head takes her objective - to keep Danger Mouse out of his headquarters - much too far, including hijacking his own vehicle in an attempt to run him down.

characters.name: Megahurtz
characters.description: A horned lizard creature. He's a Secret Service HQ training simulation who ends up in the real world due to Danger Mouse's meddling.

characters.name: Monsieur Aubrey le Camembear
characters.description: A bear. He's a cheese-obsessed criminal who wants to steal all the world's cheese. French Jerk: He's a Frenchman who is portrayed in a not-particularly-favourable light. National Stereotypes: He's French and has the moustache, beret, and striped shirt.

characters.name: Queen of Weevils
characters.description: A beetle. Also an evil witch from the days of Merlin. Evil Is Hammy: She speaks in an overly dramatic fashion and spends most of her screentime really chewing the scenery. Never My Fault: She blames the narrator for trapping her in the prison when she could've just ignored him.She ends up making the same mistake twice when she finally recognizes his voice."That's not fair! I wasn't ready!" Sealed Evil in a Can: She was trapped inside Merlin's staff for a thousand years.

characters.name: Spaghetti Monster
characters.description: Anthropomorphic Food: A sentient spaghetti. Food Eats You: He devours Penfold, if only temporarily. Small Role, Big Impact: Despite his limited screentime, he plays a role in driving Penfold to avoid any form of action from that point onwards.

characters.name: The Snowman
characters.description: Creepy High-Pitched Voice: Since he's voiced by Richard Ayoade, the character gets a nasally, high-pitched voice, although it's not really creepy, and more mundane than anything else. I'm Melting!: As a living snowman, he has this weakness. He even says this trope word-for-word when he gets put in Danger Mouse's car. Snowlems: He's a living, breathing snowman.

characters.name: Tsarfish
characters.description: Hidden Depths: Apparently, he's rather artistic, as shown when he holds up a drawing of his imagined bliss with Scarlett. His actual artistic skills leave a lot to be desired. Punny Name: His name is a portmanteau of "Tsar" and "starfish". This pun is reinforced by him wearing an outfit resembling Russian cossacks. Silent Antagonist: He remains mute throughout all of his appearances. Stalker with a Crush: He's one of the villains, but the main defining feature of his personality is his obsessive unrequited affection for Scarlett Johamster.

characters.name: The Coco Nostra
characters.description: A mafia group consisting of Bozorian alien clowns. They're Pom Pom's henchmen. The Mafia: ButIn London, and composed of clowns!Despite being based in London, they don't appear to be inspired byLondon Gangsters, and don't appear to offer up protection rackets. Monster Clown: As members of aClown Specieswho run a mafia, they're technically this trope, strictly speaking. Punny Name: Their name is a reference to the real-life mafia group theCosa Nostra, better known as the Sicilian Mafia.

characters.name: Pom Pom
characters.description: A clown alien from planet Bozoria. He becomes the planet's president. Hates fun and wants to make the Bozorians serious. Clown Species: He's a member of one. The Comically Serious: He has this as part of his characterisation, considering that he is a member of aClown Speciesand wishes to be taken seriously along with his entire species, missing the point that clowns are notmeantto be taken seriously. Disproportionate Retribution: Declares war on the planet Earth just because Danger Mouse mocked his species. The Don: He later becomes the don of a clown mafia based in a district of London known as Clowntown.

characters.name: Pancake
characters.description: A clown alien from planet Bozoria. One of Pom Pom's main minions and a member of The Coco Nostra. Anime Hair: He has spiky blue-and-red hair for some reason. Clown Species: He's a member of one. The Consigliere: He plays this role to Pom Pom. Signature Headgear: Wears a colourful top hat, befitting of a clown.

characters.name: Tiny Phil
characters.description: A clown alien from planet Bozoria. A member of The Coco Nostra.

characters.name: Simon The Big
characters.description: A clown alien from planet Bozoria. A member of The Coco Nostra. The Big Guy: As his epithet indicates, he is indeed the largest member of the Coco Nostra. Dumb Muscle: If anything, he's probably only in the group because he's the biggest and strongest of the rest of them. Muscles Are Meaningless: Despite his muscular appearance, he still gets captured along with the other members of the Coco Nostra anyway.

characters.name: Redhead Bozorian
characters.description: A clown alien from planet Bozoria. A member of The Coco Nostra. Evil Redhead: Given that he's a member of the Clown Mafia, this is natural. No Name Given: Unlike the other members of the Coco Nostra, he doesn't have a name.

characters.name: Hydrant
characters.description: An organization of evil lizards led by Hissteria. Reptiles Are Abhorrent: After all, they are a terrorist group composed of lizards. Shout-Out: Their name is a reference to the terrorist group H.Y.D.R.A from Marvel Comics and also a pun on fire hydrants.

characters.name: Hissteria
characters.description: A lizard. The leader of Hydrant. Arch-Enemy: To Jeopardy Mouse. Floating Platforms: Similarly to Marvel's Silver Surfer, she rides around on one of these. Foil: She's one to Baron Greenback, oddly enough. Whereas Baron Greenback has a noble title, Hissteria lacks a noble title. Also, whereas Greenback only has a handful of henchmen at his beck and call, Hissteria has an entire army of terrorists at her command. While the Baron is an amphibian, Hissteria is a reptile. My Nayme Is: Her name is spelled as "Hysteria" in the Netflix subtitles.

characters.name: Professor Ham Hands
characters.description: A pig. He works for Hydrant. Sinister Swine: A pig who works for a major anarchist group.

characters.name: Scarlett Johamster
characters.description: A hamster. She's a film star who becomes Penfold's girlfriend. Damsel in Distress: She gets kidnapped by Penfold'sEvil Counterpartfrom the Twystyverse, Baron Silas von Penfold, who wishes to force her to marry him and make her his queen consort. Deconstructed in that this isn't the first time this has happened, and the various times she gets kidnapped by supervillains forces her to break up with Penfold. Famed in Story: She's a beloved celebrity and actress. No Celebrities Were Harmed: She's obviously intended as a reference to American actress Scarlett Johanssen. Normie Dates a Celebrity: This is the basis for her relationship with Penfold.

characters.name: Derek Mallard
characters.description: A mouse. Danger Mouse's future descendant. Non-Indicative Name: He's a mouse, not a duck. Ret-Gone: After theBad Future(Danger Mouse acccidentally destroying Earth) is prevented, Derek is erased because the timeline he's from no longer exists.

characters.name: Pennyfold
characters.description: A hamster. Penfold's future descendant. Her father refused to let her marry Derek Mallard until Derek could fix what Danger Mouse did. Parental Marriage Veto: Her father doesn't want her to marry Derek Mallard, and can apparently stop her from doing so. Ret-Gone: After theBad Future(Danger Mouse acccidentally destroying Earth) is prevented, Penny is erased because the timeline she's from no longer exists.

characters.name: Professor Squawkencluck's Mum
characters.description: A chicken. She's a scientist like her daughter. Aesop Amnesia: She promises never to genetically-alter her husband's DNA after he's defeated; however, given that he appears one more time in the series, it's clear she hasn't learnt her lesson. Generation Xerox: Looks like an older version of her daughter. It Runs in the Family: Presumably, the Professor inherited her scientific talent from her. Mad Scientist: She has elements of this, including tampering with genetic engineering to an unhealthy extent, such asaltering her own husband's DNA.

characters.name: Ichabod Mouse
characters.description: A mouse. Danger Mouse's great-great-great-great uncle who stopped the Headless Postman's reign of terror. Adaptational Badass: Apparently, considering that the character he was named after was in fact a superstitious fool who fled from the sight of theHeadless Horsemanand may or may not have survived the events of the story, leading to the narrative the people of Sleepy Hollow tell about him "spirited" off by the Horseman. Ichabod, on the other hand, is implied to have been a very capable and heroic personage. Famous Ancestor: Danger Mouse's famous ancestor, to be precise. Generation Xerox: While he never appears on-screen, if we are to assume that genetics in the Dangermouseverse works in a similar manner to ancestry as it is depicted in most cartoons, he would presumably bear a resemblance to his descendant. The Ghost: Never shown on-screen, but his presence is felt simply from the reverent way the Danger Agents talk about him.

characters.name: Dane G. Mouse
characters.description: A mouse. He and his life are a simulation created by Megahurtz to trap Danger Mouse. Lotus-Eater Machine: Megahertz created Dane and his world in attempt to trap DM and make him think he imagined his life as a Danger Agent. Punny Name: Danger Mouse

characters.name: Merlin
characters.description: A goat. He's a medieval wizard. Attention Deficit... Ooh, Shiny!: This is hisFatal Flaw. Because he's been asleep for more than a millennium, he remains fascinated by the sleek new technology of modern Britain to the point where it easily becomes a distraction. King in the Mountain: He slept for a thousand years until he could be awakened, and somehow managed to remain alive - presumably due to his magic - despite all this. Really 700 Years Old: More like a thousand. Rip Van Winkle: He slept for over a millennium after defeating the Weevil Queen, during which time his tomb became a popular tourist attraction.He's later awaken from his slumber by Danger Mouse and Penfold in order to prevent corrupt alien merchant Quark from selling parts of his staff.

characters.name: Bernand
characters.description: A teddy bear. He belongs to Penfold. Bernand was brought to life by Mr. Snuggles, and when he made up with Dawn, Bernand went back to being non-sentient. Living Toys: Like Mr Snuggles, he's a magic teddy bear brought to life.

characters.name: Major Mugsy
characters.description: A teddy bear. Owned by Colonel K.

characters.name: The Queen
characters.description: A corgi. She's the queen of the United Kingdom. Fatal Flaw: When she's seen, she's knighting Colonel K for the many years he's devoted to running the Danger Agency, only to accidentally cut his arm off, this being apparently not the first time this has happened. However, fortunately, Colonel K isn't actually there in person — he projected a holograph of himself rather than coming to the Palace himself. The High Queen: Since she's the Queen of the United Kingdom and the one who approves of the Danger Agency, she embodies this trope. When Danger Mouse defeats the Safety Mice and Baron Greenback, she enthusiastically cheers him on. No Celebrities Were Harmed: She's a version of the late Queen Elizabeth II, Queen of the United Kingdom. Reasonable Authority Figure: Despite her limited screentime, she's nothing but kind.

characters.name: Big Mike
characters.description: A hippo. He's the proprietor of Big Mike's Pie Stall outside Danger HQ. The main cast buys from him often. Inexplicably Identical Individuals: There's a hot-dog vendor in America who looks just like him. We only see this counterpart once, when, due to a device Baron von Greenback uses to put the physical and political geography of the world into disorder, Britain becomes merged with the United States.

characters.name: Professor Jellyfishowitz
characters.description: A jellyfish. He travels in a motorized fish tank.

characters.name: Granny Penfold
characters.description: Cool Old Lady: She instructed Penfold in the art of farm fu. Old Master: Despite being British, she's a parody of the kind of wise old master trope which is common to the wuxia genre. The fact that her home is styled in a manner resembling a Chinese-Dutch farm more than a British farm would imply that Penfold is of such ancestry. Posthumous Character: She's presumably deceased by the time the main series starts.

characters.name: Pinfold
characters.description: A hamster. Penfold's cousin from New Zealand. Camera Fiend: As a tourist, he loves to take photographs of beloved landmarks. Generation Xerox: He bears a striking resemblance to Penfold. Hawaiian-Shirted Tourist: Averted, since he wears a simple green shirt rather than a coloured Hawaiian shirt. Punny Name: His name is Penfold's name pronounced with an Antipodean accent.

characters.name: Mr. Huckold
characters.description: A vague bird. He's a chemistry teacher.

characters.name: Jimmy Camel
characters.description: A camel. He's a chat show host. Flat Character: He's a beloved celebrity within the Dangermouseverse but he isn't developed as a character in any significant way. The Host: That's his job. No Celebrities Were Harmed: He's a parody of the real-life talk show host Jimmy Kimmel. The Talk Show with Host Name: He runs theJimmy Camel Show.

characters.name: Lionel
characters.description: A giant spider. He isn't anthropomorphic, but is still intelligent and can talk. He maintains the World Wide Web, a giant spider web which creates the internet. The Bus Came Back: Returns as one of the enemies Quark forces the heroes to battle. Don't Wake the Sleeper: He's been asleep for years, but the fact that Penfold accidentally woke him up spells trouble for the safety of the world. E.T. Gave Us Wi-Fi: Apparently, he was the one responsible for the creation of the World Wide Web in the Dangermouseverse, and then fell asleep afterwards. Giant Spider: He happens to be one. Unlike most examples of this trope, including Rowling'sAragog, he happens to be a very friendly kind of giant spider.

characters.name: Tour Guide
characters.description: A springbok. She's an Australian tour guide who leads tours in many continents. Flat Character: All she is is a tour guide, and she's Australian, but that's it. Hidden Depths: Apparently she's good with crossword puzzles, since she notices the crossword puzzle on the newspaper Stilletto gets wrapped in. Misplaced Wildlife: Oddly, despite being a springbok, she has an Australian accent. Springboks are not native to Australia, they are native to the African continent. Offscreen Teleportation: Appears in many countries around the world, including Britain. One has to assume she does a lot of flying for her job.

characters.name: Selfie Guy
characters.description: A walrus. He's a recurring tourist on the tour guide's tours and keeps taking selfies with various threats.

characters.name: The Wappos
characters.description: Alien tourists who come to Earth to watch Danger Mouse's heroics.

characters.name: Sinister Mouse
characters.description: A mouse. Danger mouse's evil twin. Red and Black and Evil All Over: His suit and eyes are red, and his eyepatch is black. Red Eyes, Take Warning: Like the other Danger Agency's members' Twystyverse counterparts, Sinister Mouse had red eyes.

characters.name: Sinister Moth
characters.description: A moth. Danger Moth's evil twin. Batman Can Breathe in Space: She casually flies around outside Earth's atmosphere. Dark Is Evil: She is grey, while Danger Moth is beige. Moth Menace: Played straight, given that she's theEvil Counterpartto Danger Moth. Red Eyes, Take Warning: Like all the Twystyverse villains.

characters.name: Criminal K
characters.description: A chinchilla. Colonel K's evil twin. Non-Standard Character Design: His and Silas von Penfold's pupils have a weird diamond shape, while all the other characters (including the other Twystyverse ones) have round pupils. Red Eyes, Take Warning: He's Colonel K's evil twin and has red sclerae.

characters.name: Twysty-Squawkencluck
characters.description: A chicken. Squawkencluck's evil twin. Evil Counterpart: To Professor Squawkencluck. Noodle Incident: It's not explained how she became old around the same time her good counterpart was aged down. White Hair, Black Heart: Since her counterpart in the main universe had been de-aged at the time of her debut, Twysty-Squawk appeared elderly instead.

characters.name: Baron Silas von Penfold
characters.description: A hamster. Penfold's evil twin. Aristocrats Are Evil: As with Baron von Greenback in the main universe, he's an aristocrat in this one and plain evil. However, oddly, he still holds onto the nobiliary particle "von" despite not even being German. Evil Counterpart: He's Penfold's evil counterpart, to be precise. Non-Standard Character Design: His and Criminal K's pupils have a weird diamond shape, while all the other characters (including the other Twystyverse ones) have round pupils. Red Eyes, Take Warning: He's Penfold's evil twin and a criminal mastermind, and his sclerae are red.

characters.name: Twysty-Nero
characters.description: A caterpillar. Baron Silas von Penfold's pet. Amazing Technicolor Population: He's purple with darker purple spots for some reason.

characters.name: Twysty-Big Mike
characters.description: A hippo. Counterpart of Big Mike, and owns a vegetable stall as opposed to Big Mike's pie stall.
